references_named: Roland Barthes, The Death of the Author (1967)
rationale: The mechanism is the argument: a contenteditable article whose first keystroke strikes the author's byline through, made browser-mechanical via beforeinput, and whose lack of persistence lets reload resurrect him unmarked. This is a strong P1 read — Barthes's claim is wired to the cursor, not quoted at it. The 'resurrection on reload' turn is the cheerful-cynic payload: the web both grants and silently revokes authorship, which lands as a critique of Barthes via the refresh button. Restrained single-file build, dry tone, open licence, no storage, and a fresh literary-theory angle for a catalogue that leans on visual-art lineage.
reservations: contenteditable-as-material is well-trodden net.art territory, so novelty rests heavily on the Barthes framing rather than on the affordance itself; the chance/order axis (P5) is invoked but remains a bit decorative in the actual page — the mechanism is more about presence/absence of the author than about order vs. entropy in any visible way.
revision_suggestion: Consider a small generative or stochastic element on first load (e.g., a randomized Barthes quote, or a different 'author' name drawn from a list, or a slight procedural variation in the struck-through styling) so the chance axis has a real per-visit behavior rather than being only an interpretive frame.
